description: A team's average wins is the average of the wins in its individual manager-half rows.

c.request: Using the manager_half data, which teams have above-average average wins? For each team, show its average wins, its average of (games managed minus losses) divided by losses (ignoring missing values), and how far its average wins is above the mean across teams. Give the top 10 by that gap, highest first (missing last), unrounded. A team's average wins is the average of the wins in its individual manager-half rows.
c.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(w) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_wins FROM t) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_wins - m.mean_wins AS gap FROM t CROSS JOIN m WHERE t.avg_wins > m.mean_wins ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

b.request: Using manager_half, group rows by team_id and compute each team's average wins as the mean of w across its manager-half rows, then compute each team's average of (g - l) / l over rows where l is non-null and nonzero, and the gap as the team's average wins minus the mean of the per-team average wins across all teams; keep only teams whose gap is above zero, and return the top 10 by gap in descending order (nulls last) with unrounded values
b.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(w) AS avg_wins, AVG(CASE WHEN l IS NOT NULL AND l <> 0 THEN (g - l) * 1.0 / l END) AS avg_g_minus_l_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), x AS (SELECT team_id, avg_wins, avg_g_minus_l_ratio, avg_wins - (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM t) AS gap FROM t) SELECT team_id, avg_wins, avg_g_minus_l_ratio, gap FROM x WHERE gap > 0 ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

a.request: In `manager_half`, for each team (`team_id`), compute its average wins per manager_half record (one record per manager, half and season) and its average of (games managed − losses) ÷ losses, ignoring missing values. Keep the teams whose average wins is above the mean of all teams' average wins. Return the team id, the average wins, the average (games − losses) ÷ losses, and how far the average wins is above that mean. Sort by that gap from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.
a.sql: WITH team_avg AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(w) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_wins FROM team_avg) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_wins - o.mean_wins AS gap FROM team_avg t CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE t.avg_wins > o.mean_wins ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Using the manager_half data, which teams have an above-average average number of wins? Here a team's average wins is the average of the wins across its individual manager-half rows. For each team, show its average wins, its average of (games managed minus losses) divided by losses (ignoring missing values), and how far its average wins is above the mean of average wins across all teams. Give the top 10 teams by that gap, highest first (missing values last), unrounded.
d.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(w) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id) SELECT team_id, avg_wins, avg_ratio, avg_wins - (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM t) AS gap FROM t WHERE avg_wins > (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM t) ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10
